arguments.decision: How should the repository's TypeScript scripts and tests (scripts/*.ts and the clean-code skill scripts), written against the Deno namespace, run on Node.js 24.19?

candidates.description: Preload @deno/shim-deno as globalThis.Deno and add local glue: a Deno.test adapter onto node:test that passes name and origin, and a local Deno.Command class on node:child_process with output() and spawn(). Existing Deno.* call sites stay unchanged; only the Deno.execPath spawns of Deno subcommands change.

Preload @deno/shim-deno as globalThis.Deno in a two-line module, so the file-system, env, args, exit and errors call sites stay unchanged; rewrite only the call sites the shim cannot serve: Deno.Command and Deno.CommandOutput to node:child_process, Deno.test to node:test, Deno.exitCode to process.exitCode, and the Deno.execPath spawns. No local Command or test implementation.
Rewrite every Deno.* call site to Node built-ins (node:fs/promises, node:child_process, node:test, process) and drop the Deno namespace entirely; no shim dependency and no preload.

requirements: Adds no locally owned implementation of a Deno API (no local Command or test-runner class).
Leaves call sites unchanged where an existing dependency or runtime already serves them.
arguments.priorities:
User and repository priorities (verbose-broccoli, feature/turborepo, Linear CHE-32, a trial whose result is a report; nothing is merged):
1. The user chose to move the TypeScript side from Deno to Node.js and to run the three Python packages (backfire, doc-regions, wiki-consistency) as one native uv workspace under Turborepo's experimental Python support.
2. Change only the parts that must change; leave everything else as it is. The smallest change that reaches the goal wins.
3. AGENTS.md reuse order: first existing repository, runtime, standard-library or dependency functionality; then a stable upstream dependency; then an unstable upstream with the smallest patch; last, minimal glue. Minimize locally owned code; prefer reducing locally owned implementation over reducing dependency count. If the goal needs substantial new local implementation, stop and report instead.
4. Requirements that stay: built backfire plugins install offline, stay self-contained and write only into their own .venv; readiness proves the server runs from its own .venv.
5. Dropping a check, changing scope, changing governance documents, or changing the user's global tools (Node, npm, uv, Codex) is the user's decision, not the agent's.
